rulings.ruling: Confirmed as proposed. Gamma at a reference date credits every counted week whose first day is on or before it, so the week containing the reference counts as observed at its observed adherence; Gamma at a week start credits every counted week whose last day is before it; the same reference-date rule applies to Gamma(t_A) and Gamma(t_B). The decomposition O / U / F is correct: O is inside the current estimate and is never added; g = U + F = Gamma(t_RW) - Gamma(t_ref). Chief's check reproduces (U 0.01648 + F 0.02119 = 0.03767; U 0 + F 0.01511; U 0.00711 + F 0.00800 = 0.01511; one-week overcount at most 0.00761 / 0.00476 / 0.00285 log time). All ten r1 forecast examples recompute to the same seconds, status and flags (workedExamples.forecast, reproducesR1ForecastSeconds).
rulings.basis: Arithmetic and sporting judgement on the error direction
rulings.confidence: HIGH for the direction and the one-week bound; the magnitudes they bound remain placeholders
rulings.rationale: A reference reflects the training done before it. Leaving the part of its week before the date uncredited at t_ref and crediting it later as unobserved gain adds back training already inside the measured result: an over-fast error, the harmful direction (RFC01). Crediting the whole week instead leaves uncredited at most the days after the reference in that week: a slow-side bias of at most one week. V1RC reads a reference only from the week after it is dated and recorded, so the reference week is always complete and its adherence is observed, never assumed. For the pair both endpoints use the same rule, so dGamma keeps its length and is never computed with mixed rules. Example A1-1 shows the difference: same inputs as (d) with B mid-week give the (d) range under r2 and a 1:52:00 central (1 min faster) under the r1 rule.
conditions: If a reference could ever be read inside the week that contains it, re-review (not possible under the V1RC cutoff today).

rulings.topic: Plan scenario versus observed forecast; statistical reading
rulings.ruling: planScenario admissible once history exists: its past is factual (U at observed adherence) and only its future is conditional, which its wording names; it describes what the plan offers, not this athlete's behaviour, and its slow edge still assumes no further improvement. observedForecast from 2 completed counted weeks: approved. Coincidence: one range when f(mean a) = 1 or when both rounded triplets are identical (kind OBSERVED_FORECAST, coincidesWithPlanScenario true). Labelling approved: interval {kind PLAUSIBILITY_ENVELOPE, probabilistic false, calibrated false}; z is a spread constant, never a coverage.
rulings.evidenceStatus: PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN (the 2-week threshold); the labelling is a statement of what the model is, not an evidence claim
rulings.basis: Sporting judgement and statistics; placeholder for the threshold
rulings.rationale: The scenario answers a legitimate question, what the plan offers if followed, and its condition is stated; after low adherence it is faster than the observed forecast, which is why it is never the headline when the observed forecast is shown (the fast edge read as an expectation is the risk r1 F11 named). One week of adherence is noisy: in a three-run week one missed session moves a by about a third. Two weeks halve the leverage of any one session; waiting longer leaves only the optimistic scenario on screen for longer. The envelope is not a probability interval: its slow edge is a deterministic no-gain anchor, its fast edge a prior quantile of R times a fixed ceiling, and no coverage has been measured (r1 C5). Calling it a probability or confidence interval would claim a calibration that does not exist.
conditions: Both ranges carry every r1 rule: withdrawal, slowdown and Q8-down g = 0 (adherence never overrides them), horizon, own width test, never narrowed, range first, central never alone.
Observed forecast first when both are shown; the plan scenario is the conditional alternative, never the headline while the observed forecast is SHOWN.
No copy presents a range as a probability, chance, likelihood, coverage percentage or confidence interval; z is never displayed.
The scenario wording never refers to a past shortfall.
Flag ASSUMES_PLAN_FOLLOWED is retired: the kind PLAN_SCENARIO carries that meaning (examples f, A2-1).

rulings.topic: Pace Insights: athlete-confirmed pace revision without a test or race
rulings.disposition: MODIFY: APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS as an explicitly reversible, limited recommendation for THRESHOLD_CONTROLLED only; REFUSE for FIVE_K_EFFORT, TEN_K_EFFORT, HALF_MARATHON_EFFORT and MARATHON_EFFORT; sub-question (reps >= 3 min voting in 5K/10K) REFUSED. Conditional on escalation E1; without it A3 is REFUSE and r1 F9 stands.
rulings.ruling: Several comparable threshold sessions at the target effort may support an athlete-confirmed revision of the threshold band only: step min(median margin over all voting executions, 2%), total at most 3% over the V1RC band in force (its Q8 factor included), at most one step per 28 days, effective at the next week boundary, ended at once by any harder-than-cue execution of the domain and the other listed signals, lapsing after 56 days unless the domain is then STABLE or IMPROVING against it. It changes only the threshold band shown and read by the RWS selector, never capacity, estimates, the forecast, tests, the goal comparison, dose, progression, phase or eligibility. The race-pace domains keep the r1 F9 route: a qualifying test or race is the only way their paces move beyond the V1RC rule. The gap between the desired and the sustained capability is recorded in escalations.
rulings.evidenceStatus: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (training data and effort cues carry information about threshold-domain change at group level: V1RC SRC06, SRC22); PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN (an individual revision magnitude from a few sessions); SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (refusal: rep pace above critical speed depends on D' and its reconstitution, not on continuous capacity alone: RFC19, RFC20, V1RC SRC07)
rulings.basis: Literature for the direction and the domain line; sporting judgement for every number (placeholders)
rulings.rationale: Threshold: work in long bouts (each >= 5 min, >= 15 min in total) at speeds sustainable for 55-75 min, below critical speed (V1RC SRC07), where pace at a stable effort is close to a steady-state readout. Effort and speech cues follow threshold change with training (the last positive talk-test stage tracked the ventilatory threshold after training, V1RC SRC22), and training data carry capacity information (critical speed from training logs related to marathon performance, V1RC SRC06), but with about 8% error at the individual level, so the change is a band, not a capacity; each step is no larger than the athlete's own median in-cue margin; and the athlete confirms. Counterevidence: perceptual cues err toward under-reading intensity above threshold (V1RC SRC22: predictive errors biased toward passing the talk test above VT), so an athlete chasing a too-fast band can still report an in-cue effort. A single harder-than-cue execution ends the revision because V1RC Q8 would not catch this failure: Q8 reads the V1RC band, and the athlete is now faster than it. Race-pace domains: their bands are the race-pace estimates, used by race-pace touches (raceTouchUsesEventDomain) and, for the half and marathon, next to race-day pacing. Moving them from training would let a race pace run ahead of the capacity the estimates support: the costly fast-start error (RFC01, V1RC SRC06), and the line V1RC Q8 and r1 F9 drew. 5K/10K sub-question: those speeds are at or above critical speed for most recreational runners. There, the pace a rep allows depends on the finite capacity above critical speed (D') and its reconstitution in recoveries (RFC19; runners repeated intervals at 108% of critical power with recoveries, RFC20), and self-paced rep speed depends on the session structure (RFC18). A rep at 5K effort faster than 5K race pace is expected without any capacity change, so FASTER is not a signal there; GPS distance error over short segments (3.2-6.1%, V1RC SRC13) is the size of the step. Numbers (2%, 3%, 28 and 56 days) are judgement: the step stays within one V1RC Q8 down step, and the total keeps the effective band within about 7.6% of the factor-free band in speed (example PR-1), inside the spread of recreational 12-week responses (RFC05 in r1: individualised group -6.2% +/- 2.8% 10-km time). V1RC rounding absorbs small steps (PR-1 round 2): the error is in the slow direction.
conditions: Escalation E1 recorded before any implementation enables it; otherwise the block is inert.
One band source: effectiveBand(THRESHOLD_CONTROLLED); the RWS selector reads it; RWS checks E1-E4 unchanged; a revision in force is labelled on the band.
Never during TAPER or RACE_WEEK (ends when either starts), and no offer within 14 days of the race.
Copy never says or implies fitter, faster race times or a new capacity; effort governs; undo always available.
No clinical inference from any ending signal; adverse responses route through the existing V1RC/engine paths only.
Re-review on the first real revision data (sessions after a revision versus later tests or races) or any adverse event in a threshold session with a revision in force.

aeReview.q1_currentPlanAdequate: Plan unchanged; only the target pace of one domain, within effort.
aeReview.q2_materialFact: Three or more comparable, accurately measured, in-cue executions over >= 14 days, faster than the band beyond the V1RC trigger.
aeReview.q3_keepDefensible: Yes, and it remains the default: no revision without an explicit athlete yes; effort governs either way.
aeReview.q4_changeNecessary: Not necessary for safety; a too-slow band mainly under-informs. Admissible as a reversible athlete choice.
aeReview.q5_smallestIntervention: One band, one step no larger than the athlete's own median margin and 2%, reversible at once.
aeReview.q6_smallerAlternativesInsufficient: Explain-only leaves the band behind demonstrated in-cue pace; a test is preferred and offered first when P3 offers one.
aeReview.q7_priorityAndProgression: Unchanged: no dose, progression, phase or key-session change.
aeReview.q8_evidenceSupportsDose: No dose is set; the size is bounded by observation, not by an evidence-derived dose.
aeReview.q9_uncertainty: Measurement (GPS), effort misreport and conditions; carried by TRACK/GPS-good, median, caps, and immediate ending.
aeReview.q10_askHoldClinical: No ASK or HOLD added; adverse or symptom routes unchanged.

rulings.ruling: In RACE_WEEK, up to the day before race day, the observed forecast SHOWN for the last week before RACE_WEEK may be shown frozen, after the V1RC current estimate, race-day text and pacing caution; labelled with its date; low-high only, without the central; no goal relation; never on race day or in race-day mode; never a pacing source. Not shown under any withdrawal, when it was not SHOWN, when only a plan scenario existed, when its g was 0, when the V1RC reference, its tier or a Q8 down factor changed since, for the marathon or a completion race.
rulings.rationale: r1 cut everything from RACE_WEEK because a forecast faster than the current estimate must not become a pacing reference; that risk sits on race day and on a single time (the central) and grows if the range moves in race week. A dated, frozen range without its central, placed after the pacing caution, carries the information of the week before and adds no new claim. With no counted week left its gain is the unobserved gain of training already done (F = 0; example A4-1). Race day and the goal relation are excluded because that is where a number becomes a pace (RFC01; V1RC SRC06: a fast first half relative to capacity was associated with marked slowdown).
conditions: The pacing caution remains V1RC's: start at or slower than the slower end of the current estimate.
Only the observed forecast is frozen: in race week no counted week remains for a plan scenario's condition to apply to.

rulings.disposition: APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS (sporting opinion on meaning; the formal reading of the catalog rule stays with Founder/PCG, r1 C4)
rulings.ruling: A positional relation FASTER_THAN_RANGE / INSIDE_RANGE / SLOWER_THAN_RANGE against the rounded displayed low and high (inclusive), never the central, beside each SHOWN range under its own condition, with the neutral text in values; the V1RC goal comparison with the current estimate stays primary and first. Not in race week, not for the marathon, not when no range is shown. The goal is never evidence and changes nothing.
rulings.evidenceStatus: N/A (a comparison of two displayed numbers)
rulings.rationale: A position relative to a range whose slow edge assumes no gain is a fact about two numbers, not a prediction. FASTER_THAN_RANGE is useful realism and discourages pacing to the goal; SLOWER_THAN_RANGE is harmless. INSIDE_RANGE is the one a reader turns into "achievable", which is why the words and styling stay neutral, the comparison with the current estimate (which says whether the goal needs improvement) stays first, and race week is excluded. Per range, because "inside the plan scenario" and "faster than the observed forecast" can both be true (examples A5-b-4730) and each is only true under its own condition.
conditions: No success or failure styling (colour, icon, check) on the relation.
Never "on track", "achievable", "likely" or a probability.
The goal never feeds anything (C2).

rulings.disposition: APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS; MODIFY (continuous TIME steps earn extent credit like DISTANCE steps; an unfinished repetition earns 0; a recorded distance is used when steps are missing; extent only, never intensity)
rulings.ruling: Per-session credit c in [0, 1]: missing report 0; completed (the engine's reading) 1; not completed with RWS steps: planning-share weighted extent over WORK and STEADY steps (met 1; an unfinished repetition 0; any other unmet WORK or STEADY step its measured extent fraction in its own unit); not completed without usable steps: the recorded distance fraction for a distance-target session, else the r1 minutes reading. a_w weights by planned minutes.
rulings.evidenceStatus: SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (adaptation depends on the training dose received: RFC10); PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN (this specific reading)
rulings.basis: Sporting judgement; conservative for the forecast
rulings.rationale: The forecast's adherence is a proxy for the stimulus received and must err low. With completion by target, the engine's completed reading is the right credit for completed sessions, slower or faster. For unfinished distance-target sessions minutes misread the extent: a slower runner reaches the planned minutes short of the distance. The extent fraction removes that over-credit (AD-1: S3 reads 0.75, not 1). Trade-off, stated: the canonical dose is minutes, and a slower runner who ran the planned minutes received about the planned time at effort; the extent reading under-credits them, which only slows the fast edge, the safe direction for a forecast. The proposal's binary reading of an unmet continuous TIME step (0 for 15 of 20 min) was inconsistent with its fractional DISTANCE reading and is replaced by the extent fraction (S4: 0.75). An unfinished repetition stays 0: it is the unit of an interval session. When steps are missing but a distance is recorded, the distance is used for the same reason (S3-noSteps).
conditions: targetMet must mean the step's extent target only. If the final RWS contract makes it include intensity, use the measured extent fraction instead (Data/Engineering confirm).
A6 depends on a non-final RWS contract: any change to completed, steps, kinds or weights re-opens A6.
Forecast credit only: never dose, progression, the engine's adherence or completion judgments, or a G03 reading (Product/UX + Data own those jointly).

rulings.ruling: Marathon: agreed, shown only as the current marathon estimate with r1 requiredText.marathon, never labelled a forecast, and also no scenario, no frozen race-week forecast and no goal relation. Plans longer than 16 weeks: NOT_YET_IN_WINDOW (one name, replacing r1 NOT_YET_IN_HORIZON and handoff HORIZON_BEYOND_LIMIT); availableFrom is the first plan week start on or after race date - 112 days (r1 example i: 2027-03-08, not 2027-03-07, because ranges change only at week boundaries). Unavailable or too-uncertain states: agreed, with the guidance never instructing a longer run, more training, a test P3 does not offer or a race entry.
rulings.rationale: An endurance gate met by doing a longer run than prescribed would be a forecast pulling training; the plan's own long runs are the route.

values.scope: Additive over COACHINGCORE-V1-RUN-CALIBRATION-FREEZE-1. No V1RC value, gate, computation or file changes. Nonclinical recreational adults, synthetic data only. paceInsights.athleteConfirmedRevision adds a separate effective-band layer for THRESHOLD_CONTROLLED only, conditional on escalation E1.

forecast.start: The V1RC current estimate of the plan's event, its unrounded {lower, central, upper} as V1RC computes them (after any Q8 down adjustment). No forecast when that estimate is UNAVAILABLE or not shown.

rules.when: No report for a planned run session
actual.completed === true (the engine's reading; under the RWS amendment completion of a distance-target session is the distance)
Not completed and RWS actual.steps with at least one WORK or STEADY step
rules.c: sum(w_s * m_s) / sum(w_s) over WORK and STEADY steps
rules.w_s: the step's planning share: target seconds for a TIME step; the midpoint of its estimated seconds for a DISTANCE step
rules.m_s: extent only, never intensity: 1 if targetMet === true; a step that is one repetition of a repeated block and not met: 0; any other WORK or STEADY step not met (continuous TIME or DISTANCE): min(1, measured extent / target extent) in its own unit (seconds or metres) when measured, else 0

rules.when: Not completed, no usable steps, distance-target session with a recorded distance

rules.c: min(actual minutes, planned minutes) / planned minutes
rules.note: r1 reading; 0 if no extent is recorded

adherence.weekly: a_w = sum(planned minutes x c) / sum(planned minutes), planned minutes = prescription.durationMinutes (the canonical planning dose)
adherence.weekWithoutPlannedRunMinutes: Not counted (0 credit) and left out of the mean
adherence.futureMeanOf: a (the weekly adherence), then f applied once
adherence.scope: Credit for the forecast only. It never feeds dose, progression, the engine's adherence or completion judgments, or any G03 reading (Product/UX + Data own those).

response.pair: One pair: A = the earliest eligible reference dated on or after (plan start - 28 days); B = the current V1RC standard reference. Same kind (RACE_RESULT with RACE_RESULT; TIME_TRIAL or FIELD_TEST with TIME_TRIAL or FIELD_TEST). Neither presumed, SUBMAXIMAL_LOWER_BOUND, unknown effort, OUTSIDE_MODEL_POPULATION, nor longer than the half marathon. No declared break of 7 days or more between A and B.
response.sigma: The V1RC margin of each reference (tier margin plus any slow-runner margin) / 1.2816
response.update: R_obs = ln(T10_A / T10_B) / dGamma; var = (sigma_A^2 + sigma_B^2) / dGamma^2; R_c = (R_c0/s0^2 + R_obs/var) / (1/s0^2 + 1/var); sd = (1/s0^2 + 1/var)^(-1/2); then R_c clipped to [0, 1]. No pair: R_c = 0.5, sd = 0.3.

slowdown.comparedWith: the most recent eligible same-kind reference dated before B (pair rules except spacing)
slowdown.effect: g = 0 until a later reference is not 3% slower

formulas.H_eff: sum of f(a_w) over credited counted plan weeks (fc.weekCredit); each future counted week before RACE_WEEK earns f(future adherence of the range): 1 for the plan scenario, f(mean a) for the observed forecast
formulas.g: Gamma(start of RACE_WEEK) - Gamma(reference date), per range; 0 for the marathon, after a slowdown, or while a Q8 down factor is in force

forecast.rounding: V1RC roundOutwardSeconds (5K/10K 15 s, half/marathon 60 s): low floored, high ceiled, central to nearest
forecast.width: rounded high / rounded low - 1; shown only if <= wMax, else TOO_UNCERTAIN_TO_SHOW; never narrowed
forecast.shownUntil: Live ranges: the day before RACE_WEEK starts. In RACE_WEEK: only fc.raceWeek.

confidence.withoutGain: the current estimate tier, at most MODERATE

forecast.recompute: At the week boundary only; withdrawal applies at once
withdrawal: declared break of 14 days or more
event estimate unavailable or not shown
extension or ESTIMATE boundary not enabled

requiredText.observedForecast: If you keep training as you have over the last <n> weeks, <race> on <date>: <low>-<high>. The slower end assumes no further improvement. Not a promise.
requiredText.planScenario: If you follow the plan from now on, <race> on <date>: <low>-<high>. The slower end assumes no further improvement. Not a promise.
requiredText.coincide: If you keep training as you have over the last <n> weeks, in line with the plan, <race> on <date>: <low>-<high>. The slower end assumes no further improvement. Not a promise.
requiredText.basis: Based on your <reference> of <date>; individual results vary. A plausible span, not a probability.
requiredText.raceWeek: Forecast of <date>, not updated in race week: <low>-<high>. For pacing, use your current estimate and its caution.
requiredText.goal: Your goal <time> is faster than / within / slower than this range.
requiredText.notYetInWindow: A forecast appears from <availableFrom>, 16 weeks before the race. Until then, your current estimate.
requiredText.marathon: Your current marathon estimate, assuming the block's long runs are completed: <low>-<high>. No further improvement is assumed for the marathon. Not a promise.

weekCredit.atReferenceDate: Gamma(d) at a reference date d credits every counted plan week whose first day is on or before d: the week that contains the reference is credited at its observed adherence (a reference dated before the plan credits nothing).
weekCredit.atWeekStart: Gamma(t) at a week start t (t_now = start of the week in force; t_RW = start of RACE_WEEK) credits every counted plan week whose last day is before t.
weekCredit.pair: Gamma(t_A) and Gamma(t_B) of the response pair use atReferenceDate.
weekCredit.referenceWeekAdherence: Always observed: V1RC reads a reference only from the week after it is dated and recorded, so the week containing it is complete.

decomposition.O: ln(T10_A / T10_B): observed gain, already inside the V1RC current estimate; never added
decomposition.U: Gamma(t_now) - Gamma(t_ref): executed weeks after the reference, at observed adherence, not yet measured
decomposition.F: Gamma(t_RW) - Gamma(t_now): counted weeks still to come before RACE_WEEK, at the range's future adherence
decomposition.g: U + F = Gamma(t_RW) - Gamma(t_ref); 0 for the marathon, after a slowdown, or while a Q8 down factor is in force (both ranges)

observedForecast.futureAdherence: mean a of the last <= 4 completed counted weeks, then f once

ranges.coincide: If f(mean a) = 1, or the rounded [low, central, high] of both ranges are identical: one range, kind OBSERVED_FORECAST, coincidesWithPlanScenario true
ranges.eachRange: Own width test against wMax, shown whole or TOO_UNCERTAIN_TO_SHOW, never narrowed; same slow edge (current estimate upper), same R_c and R_hi, same g = 0 rules
ranges.presentation: When both are shown: the observed forecast first, the plan scenario as the conditional alternative; the plan scenario is never the headline while the observed forecast is SHOWN; range first, central never alone. If only the observed forecast passes the width test, only it is shown.
ranges.zMeaning: z = 1.2816 is a spread constant on the response prior; never displayed, never described as a coverage, a percentage or a probability

retiredFlags.ASSUMES_PLAN_FOLLOWED: replaced by the range kind PLAN_SCENARIO

notYetInWindow.availableFrom: the first plan week start on or after (race date - 112 days)

raceWeek.frozenForecast: The observed forecast that was SHOWN for the last week before RACE_WEEK (including the coincide case), frozen: never recomputed, no gain added
raceWeek.shownThrough: the day before race day; never on race day or in race-day mode

display.position: after the V1RC current estimate, its race-day text and its pacing caution
display.label: Forecast of <date>; not updated in race week

notShownIf: the observed forecast was not SHOWN for that week (TOO_UNCERTAIN_TO_SHOW, UNAVAILABLE, NOT_ENOUGH_HISTORY, plan scenario only)
its g was 0 (it equals the current estimate)
the V1RC reference in force differs from the one it was computed from, its confidence tier changed, or a Q8 down factor took effect since

forecast.marathonPresentation: Shown only as the current marathon estimate with requiredText.marathon; never labelled a forecast; no plan scenario, no observed forecast, no race-week frozen forecast and no goal relation to a range (the V1RC goal comparison only)

goal.primary: The V1RC goal comparison with the current estimate, unchanged and always first

relationToRange.against: the rounded displayed low and high of each SHOWN range, inclusive (low <= goal <= high is INSIDE_RANGE); never the central
relationToRange.perRange: stated beside its own range under that range's condition

forecast.unavailableGuidance: Unavailable, too-uncertain and not-yet-in-window states state the V1RC reason and name only existing V1RC routes: report a race result at the event distance (never a prompt to enter one), or the P3 field test only when assessment.status is OFFERED. Never instruct a longer run, more training, a test P3 does not offer, or a race entry; the plan's own sessions are the route to the endurance gates.
forbiddenInCopy: a coverage or percentage attached to a range
success or failure styling of the goal relation

paceInsights.comparable: V1RC comparableRun (no HEAT, HILLY, TRAIL, WIND_STRONG; no treadmill; GPS not poor), completed, RPE inside the cue, every work bout >= 5 min
paceInsights.classify: As V1RC Q8 against the band in force in the execution's own week: FASTER if fast edge pace / pace - 1 > 0.015; SLOWER if pace / slow edge pace - 1 > 0.015; else INSIDE

voteMinWorkBoutMinutes.note: Unchanged from r1; reps of 3-5 min never vote in any domain (A3 sub-question refused)

athleteConfirmedRevision.conditionalOn: Escalation E1 recorded by Chief/Founder; if it is not, this block is inert and r1 F9 applies unchanged

refusedDomains.FIVE_K_EFFORT: race-pace domain; rep pace above critical speed is not a capacity readout
refusedDomains.HALF_MARATHON_EFFORT: race-pace domain used for race-pace touches and next to race-day pacing
refusedDomains.MARATHON_EFFORT: race-pace domain; the marathon is where a fast estimate costs most

offeredWhen: Insights state IMPROVING for the domain (r1 rules), computed at the week boundary, every execution classified against the effective band in force in its own week
V1RC Q8 factor for the domain in force at its +0.045 cap; band AVAILABLE with basis DERIVED_FROM_CAPACITY (never an observed P2 band)

every voting execution: comparable (r1), completed, RPE inside the cue and response compatible (V1RC onTarget), measurement TRACK, or GPS with quality GOOD (not merely not poor), every work bout >= 5 min and total work >= 15 min (V1RC Q8 rule)
every voting execution dated on or after the effective date of the previous revision step in the domain (no execution supports two steps)
no harder-than-cue execution of the domain among the window's executions, and no adverse response on any run in the 7 days before the offer
plan mode EASY; no hold; no declared break >= 7 days in the window; warning-sign screen not REQUIRED; experience not NONE
not in TAPER, RACE_WEEK or POST_EVENT, and not within 14 days before the race date
at least 28 days since the effective date of the previous step, or since a revision ended
athleteConfirmedRevision.offerOrder: When P3 offers a field test now, the test is offered first and the revision is the alternative, with the statement that a test or race updates every pace and estimate, the revision only this band

step.rule: min(median over all voting executions of (effective fast edge pace / execution pace - 1), 0.02, 0.03 - revision in force)

athleteConfirmedRevision.application: Speed terms, as V1RC Q8: effective fast edge = paceEdge((1 / V1RC fastSecondsPerKm) x (1 + R), 5); effective slow edge = max(paceEdge((1 / V1RC slowSecondsPerKm) x (1 + R), 5), effective fast edge + 10); paceEdge = round to 0.1 s/km then up to the next multiple of 5 s/km (V1RC); R = revision in force; the V1RC band in force already includes its Q8 factor
athleteConfirmedRevision.confirmation: Athlete-confirmed only; never applied without an explicit yes; declining has no consequence and the same evidence is not offered again
athleteConfirmedRevision.effectiveFrom: the next week boundary after confirmation
endsAtOnce: any V1RC withdrawal (hold, declared break >= 7 days, WALK_JOG/RESTART/RETURN mode, warning-sign screen REQUIRED)
one comparable execution of the domain harder than the cue
two consecutive comparable executions of the domain at an in-cue effort more than 1.5% slower than the effective slow edge
Insights state SLOWER_THAN_BAND, or a V1RC Q8 down step, in the domain
an adverse response on any run
athleteConfirmedRevision.endsAtOnceMeans: for sessions not yet started; the band reverts to the V1RC band in force
athleteConfirmedRevision.lapses: At the first week boundary 56 days or more after its latest step, unless the domain state then is STABLE or IMPROVING against the effective band
athleteConfirmedRevision.changesOnly: the THRESHOLD_CONTROLLED band as shown and as read by the RWS format selector (one band source: effectiveBand); the RWS envelope checks E1-E4 unchanged
athleteConfirmedRevision.label: ATHLETE_CONFIRMED_REVISION, with the size in percent of the V1RC band and the date; effort governs
athleteConfirmedRevision.copyMustNot: say or imply fitter, faster race times, a new capacity or a test result; invite running faster than the cue
athleteConfirmedRevision.requiredText: Your last <n> threshold sessions at the target effort were faster than your band. Set your threshold band <x>% faster from <date>? Effort still governs, and you can undo this at any time. Your race estimates do not change.

workedExamples.note: Computed by a scratch Node script outside the repository (the r1 calculator, adapted) from values above; no repository code was run. Times h:mm:ss or m:ss; forecastSeconds = [low, central, high] after outward rounding. The implementation must reproduce forecastSeconds, status, display and flags exactly; intermediate values (5-6 decimals) are for debugging. Every r1 forecast example recomputes to its r1 forecastSeconds (field reproducesR1ForecastSeconds); r1 PI-1 holds unchanged by reference (threshold, Q8 room left: EXPLAIN_ONLY, no revision offered); r1 example j is replaced by A4-1 to A4-3.
workedExamples.calendar: Plans start Mon 2027-01-04; week n starts 2027-01-04 + 7(n - 1) days.

forecast.title: (a) Intermediate, 10K reference HIGH, 12 weeks to race, no individual data, adherence 0.95
forecast.inputs: As r1 example (a): Plan for a 10K, 16 weeks, starts Mon 2027-01-04; weeks 1-14 counted phases, 15 TAPER, 16 RACE_WEEK; race Sun 2027-04-25. Reference: 10K race 50:00, OFFICIAL timing, effort known, dated 2027-01-01 (pre-plan, so Gamma at the reference = 0), the only reference. Experience INTERMEDIATE. Computed at the start of week 5 (Mon 2027-02-01; race 83 days away, inside the 112-day horizon). Weeks 1-4 adherence 0.95 each. Future adherence = mean of weeks 1-4 = 0.95, f = 1. Counted weeks still to come before RACE_WEEK: 5-14 = 10.
forecast.r2Reading: f(mean a) = 1: the two ranges coincide; one range shown, kind OBSERVED_FORECAST. r1 numbers unchanged.

forecast.title: (b) As (a) with adherence 0.6
forecast.inputs: As r1 example (b): As (a) but weeks 1-4 adherence 0.6 each: f(0.6) = 0.25 per week, past H = 1.0, future 10 x 0.25 = 2.5.
forecast.r2Reading: r1 range = the observed forecast (unchanged). New: the plan scenario (past weeks at 0.6, future at 1) differs, so both are shown (A2), observed first.

forecast.title: (c) Novice, two 5K races 6 weeks apart showing improvement, 8 weeks to a 10K
forecast.inputs: As r1 example (c): Plan for a 10K, 14 weeks, starts 2027-01-04; weeks 1-12 counted, 13 TAPER, 14 RACE_WEEK; race Sun 2027-04-11. Experience NOVICE. Reference A: 5K race 30:00, OFFICIAL, 2027-01-02 (2 days before the plan, Gamma 0). Reference B: 5K race 29:00, OFFICIAL, Sun 2027-02-14 = last day of week 6 (43 days after A, same kind RACE). V1RC: no conflict (more than 28 days apart), B outside the 1.5% deadband, so B is the reference, HIGH, with the slow-runner margin (10K-equivalent 60.9 min >= 60): m = 0.035. Longest run in the last 28 days 50 min (10K gate of 40 min met). Weeks 1-6 adherence 0.9 (f = 1). Computed at the start of week 7 (Mon 2027-02-15; race 55 days away). Future counted weeks 7-12 = 6. Note: V1RC gives novices no 5 km field test (3 km only), so both references here are races, not tests.
forecast.r2Reading: B dated on the last day of week 6: the A1 rule credits the same weeks as r1. Both ranges coincide and are TOO_UNCERTAIN_TO_SHOW.

forecast.title: (d) Half-marathon athlete whose second reference is 2% slower
forecast.inputs: As r1 example (d): Plan for a half marathon, 16 weeks, starts 2027-01-04; weeks 1-14 counted, 15 TAPER, 16 RACE_WEEK; race 2027-04-25. Experience INTERMEDIATE. A: 10K race 50:00 OFFICIAL 2027-01-01. B: 10K race 51:00 OFFICIAL 2027-02-14 (end of week 6), 2.0% slower: below the 3% slowdown threshold, so the response update applies. B is the V1RC reference (44 days after A, outside the deadband), HIGH, m = 0.025. Longest run in the last 28 days 75 min (half gate 60 met). Weeks 1-6 adherence 0.95. Computed at the start of week 7; future counted weeks 7-14 = 8.

forecast.title: (d2) As (d) with B 4% slower: no gain assumed
forecast.inputs: As r1 example (d2): As (d) but B = 10K race 52:00 (4.0% slower than A, at or above the 3% threshold): g = 0, the forecast equals the current estimate, flag NO_GAIN_LATEST_RESULT_SLOWER.
forecast.r2Reading: g = 0 for both ranges (adherence never overrides a slowdown); one range, equal to the current estimate, flag NO_GAIN_LATEST_RESULT_SLOWER.

output.confidence: current estimate tier, at most MODERATE

forecast.title: (e1) Marathon that passes
forecast.inputs: As r1 example (e1): Marathon block, 16 weeks, starts 2027-01-04, race 2027-04-25, every V1RC/V1FC marathon eligibility criterion met, race day not a completion. Reference: half marathon 1:50:00 OFFICIAL 2026-12-20 (CURRENT at week 5), HIGH. Experience INTERMEDIATE. The marathon earns no training gain: the forecast is the V1RC current marathon estimate unchanged, with its caution and assumption; central 4:01:00 <= 6:00:00 (R-11 met); width 15.0% <= 0.18.
forecast.r2Reading: A7: shown only as the current marathon estimate with requiredText.marathon; never labelled a forecast; no plan scenario and no goal relation to a range.

literature.citation: Seiler S, Hetlelid KJ. The impact of rest duration on work intensity and RPE during interval training. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2005;37(9):1601-7.
literature.findingsUsed: Nine well-trained male runners, self-paced 6 x 4 min (5% incline treadmill): running velocity rose slightly from 1- to 2-min recoveries (14.4 to 14.7 km/h) with no further change at 4 min: self-selected rep speed depends on the session structure.
limitations: used as context only; the effect of rest 2-4 min was limited

literature.citation: Anderson M, Sabapathy S, Arnold B, Bellenger C, Kolodziej F, Bellinger P. The measurement and application of critical speed and D' in running: a scoping review. Sports Med 2026;56(7):1637-74.
literature.findingsUsed: 124 studies: CS is validated as the heavy/severe boundary; D' is the finite distance capacity above CS; D' reconstitution has a far smaller evidence base; CS and D' balance are strong determinants of performance from the mile to the marathon, D' balance notably at 5000 and 10,000 m.

literature.citation: Garcia-Pinillos F, Jaen-Carrillo D, Riquelme-Sebastian L, et al. Original W'-balance models do not transfer to high-intensity interval training in trained adult runners: proposal of a single-coefficient linear alternative. Physiol Rep 2026;14(20):e71152.
literature.findingsUsed: Twenty-seven trained runners repeated intervals at 108% of critical power with a 2:1 work:rest ratio to exhaustion; the number of intervals depended on individual recovery behaviour (athlete-specific recovery coefficient): interval tolerance above CS is governed by expenditure and recovery of W', not by continuous capacity alone.

literature.citation: Smyth B, Muniz-Pumares D. Calculation of critical speed from raw training data in recreational marathon runners. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2020;52(12):2637-45.
literature.findingsUsed: More than 25,000 recreational marathoners: CS from the fastest training efforts at 400-5000 m correlated with marathon performance (R about 0.67-0.70, error about 7.7-8.0%); a first half above 94% of CS was associated with marked slowdown.

literature.citation: Foster C, Porcari JP, Anderson J, et al. The talk test as a marker of exercise training intensity. J Cardiopulm Rehabil Prev 2008;28(1):24-30.
literature.findingsUsed: The intensity at the last positive talk-test stage changed with the ventilatory threshold after training and after blood donation; predictive errors were biased toward passing the talk test above VT.

literature.citation: RFC01, RFC05, RFC10 (r1 literature) and V1RC SRC05, SRC07, SRC13 (V1RC sources) are cited as settled by their records and were not re-read in this run.

an adverse event linked to race-day pacing or a suggested test
